reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Program fund creation, donation sources, and nonreversion
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (L. 2000 S.B. 721 § 192.936 through A.L. 2018 S.B. 975 & 1024 Revision; transferred 2014, formerly 192.935). Creates the Blindness Education, Screening and Treatment Program Fund from donations under sections 301.020(7) and 302.171(3) and exempts unexpended fiscal-year balances from transfer under section 33.080.

headings.title: Program development subject to available fund moneys
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Directs the department of social services, subject to fund availability, to develop a blindness education, screening, and treatment program for persons lacking adequate health benefit plan coverage.

headings.title: Required education, screening, and treatment components
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 (subdivisions (1) to (3)) and notes. Lists the three required program elements: public education on blindness and eye conditions, eye screenings and examinations, and treatment procedures necessary to prevent blindness.

headings.title: Contracting with approved nonprofit organizations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Grants the department permissive authority to contract for program development with department-approved nonprofits working in regional and community blindness education, eye donor, and vision treatment services.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority for program eligibility
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and notes. Grants the department permissive authority to adopt rules prescribing eligibility requirements for the program.

headings.title: Rulemaking compliance with chapter 536
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and notes. Conditions effectiveness of any rule or portion of a rule promulgated under section 209.015 on promulgation pursuant to chapter 536.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 6 subsections (including subsection 3 subdivisions) and history/transfer notes (L. 2000 S.B. 721 § 192.936 through A.L. 2018 S.B. 975 & 1024 Revision; transferred 2014, formerly 192.935) and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked section 301.020(7), 302.171(3), 33.080, and chapter 536 references and fund-availability qualification in subsection 2. All 6 titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: Blind pension eligibility criteria and disqualifying conditions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (subdivisions (1) to (8)) and history note (RSMo 1939 § 9451 through A.L. 2026 H.B. 2180). Covers age, character, residency, and enrollment requirements and eight disqualifications, including the $30,000 property limit (excluding home and first $100,000 in an ABLE account under sections 209.600 to 209.645), driver's license relinquishment and free chapter 302 nondriver card, vehicle operation, sighted spouse income at or above 500% FPL, soliciting alms, institutional maintenance (with conditional federal state-plan inoperability clause for mental-disease patients 65+), non-blindness, and section 209.140 violations.

headings.title: Ineligibility and termination for unexcused missed vision tests
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Makes an applicant or recipient ineligible and requires payment termination after notice and hearing opportunity for failing, without good cause or department exception, to submit to a section 209.040 vision test within thirty days of request. Separate review: Revised during review from "Termination for failing to take requested vision test" to cover both applicant ineligibility and recipient payment termination and to reflect good-cause/department exceptions and notice-and-hearing prerequisites.

headings.title: Ten-day change reporting and mail service of notices
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires reporting address, contact, and eligibility-impacting circumstance changes within ten days, treats USPS mail to the address of record as service under sections 209.010 to 209.160, and additionally requires certified mail for adverse-action notices such as hearing dates and payment terminations.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 3 subsections (including subsection 1 subdivisions (1) to (8)) and history note (RSMo 1939 § 9451 through A.L. 2026 H.B. 2180) and verified all fingerprints. Checked $30,000 property limit, $100,000 ABLE exclusion under sections 209.600 to 209.645, driver's license relinquishment and free chapter 302 card, 500% FPL sighted-spouse rule, federal state-plan inoperability clause for age 65+ mental-institution patients, and certified-mail adverse-action service. Revised subsection 2 title to cover applicant ineligibility, recipient termination, and good-cause/department exceptions; retained subsections 1 and 3.

headings.title: One-year real-property treatment of involuntary conversion proceeds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1972 S.B. 483). Treats proceeds from involuntary conversion of real property into personal property (such as condemnation, eminent domain, fire, flood, or other act of God) received while eligible for blind pensions as real property for one year from receipt.

headings.title: Meaning of receipt and condemnation-exception rule
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Defines 'receipt' for section 209.035 as actual receipt or payment into court, except that where the condemning authority files the initial exception to the commissioner's award, receipt means receipt under a final judgment.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 1972 S.B. 483) and verified all fingerprints. Checked one-year real-property treatment of involuntary conversion proceeds and the condemnation-exception definition of "receipt". Both titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: Vision standard, twelve-month duration, and certified examination
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (RSMo 1939 § 9452 through A.L. 2018 H.B. 2171). Defines 'blind' for sections 209.010 to 209.160 (corrected vision no better than 5/200 or visual field <= 5 degrees in the better eye lasting or expected to last at least twelve months) and requires a department-determined scientific vision test certified by an approved ophthalmologist, eye-disease physician, or optometrist.

headings.title: Five-year vision reexaminations, earlier requests, and exemption
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires vision recertification every fifth year or sooner upon department request or examiner indication of expected improvement, while exempting persons with no usable vision in the better eye from five-year exams unless the department has reasonable cause to request reexamination.

headings.title: Monthly pension amount, SSI ineligibility, and general-relief bar
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Provides a monthly blind pension set by appropriation at not less than $340, conditioned on being declared ineligible for federal SSI aid and not receiving general relief assistance.

headings.title: Pro rata benefit reduction when funds are insufficient
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Directs proportional pro rata reduction of each beneficiary's payments if funds available to the department of social services become insufficient to pay full benefits.

headings.title: Medical assistance funding under sections 208.151 to 208.158
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Provides that medical assistance for eligible blind recipients is payable under sections 208.151 to 208.158 without durational residence requirements, out of medical assistance funds rather than the blind pension fund.

headings.title: Annual pension setting, budget estimates, and change formula
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Directs annual legislative setting (and optional supplemental appropriation adjustment), requires department budget projections using section 209.130 tax and fund estimates, and sets the estimated-change formula. Retains source internal cross-reference 'provided in subsection 1 of this section' in the final sentence without silently repairing it to subsection 3.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 6 subsections and history note (RSMo 1939 § 9452 through A.L. 2018 H.B. 2171) and verified all fingerprints. Checked vision/duration standard, five-year and reasonable-cause reexamination rules, $340 appropriation floor with SSI/general-relief disqualifications, pro rata reduction, sections 208.151 to 208.158 medical assistance funding, and annual change formula. Confirmed source discrepancy in subsection 6 final sentence referencing "monthly pension provided in subsection 1 of this section" (while opening sentence cites subsection 3) is retained without silent correction. All 6 titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: Ineligibility of capable persons refusing work or training
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (RSMo 1939 § 9453 through A.L. 2014 H.B. 1299 Revision; prior revision 1929 § 8895). Excludes blind persons aged 18 to 50 with no occupation who are physically and mentally capable of a useful occupation or vocational/other training and refuse to engage in or avail themselves of it. Separate review: Revised during review from "Ineligibility for refusing useful occupation or training" to reflect the physical/mental capability qualification for blind persons aged 18 to 50 with no occupation; archived double-"who" phrasing retained verbatim.

headings.title: Provisional training admission and removal from pension roll
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Allows the family support division to admit an otherwise qualified applicant willing and ready to enter training, and directs striking the name from the blind pension roll if the person fails for more than a reasonable time to enter training without good cause. Separate review: Revised during review from "Provisional admission for training and removal for nonattendance" because removal applies to failing without good cause for more than a reasonable time to enter training, rather than general nonattendance.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history/prior-revision notes (RSMo 1939 § 9453 through A.L. 2014 H.B. 1299 Revision; 1929 § 8895) and verified all fingerprints. Checked age 18–50 physical/mental capability criteria and archived double-"who" phrasing in subsection 1, plus good-cause and reasonable-time qualifications for entering training in subsection 2. Revised both titles to preserve capability and failure-to-enter qualifications.

headings.title: Equal access to streets, buildings, and public places
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1941 p. 344 § 1 through A.L. 2020 S.B. 644 merged with S.B. 656). Grants persons with a disability as defined in section 213.010 the same rights to full and free use of streets, highways, sidewalks, walkways, public buildings, public facilities, and other public places.

headings.title: Equal access to public transportation, lodging, and accommodations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Entitles persons with a section 213.010 disability to full and equal accommodations and privileges in common carriers, public conveyances, hotels, lodging places, public accommodations, amusements, resorts, and public venues, subject to lawful generally applicable conditions.

headings.title: Service dog accompaniment without extra charge and damage liability
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Grants persons with a section 213.010 disability the right to be accompanied by a trained service dog as defined in section 209.200 in subsection 2 places without extra charge, while imposing liability for any damage the dog causes to premises or facilities.

headings.title: Section 209.200 definition of service dog
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Incorporates the section 209.200 definition of 'service dog' for sections 209.150 to 209.190. Separate review: Revised during review from "Cross-reference definition of service dog" to preserve the exact defining statutory cross-reference to section 209.200 for sections 209.150 to 209.190.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 4 subsections and history note (L. 1941 p. 344 § 1 through A.L. 2020 S.B. 644 merged with S.B. 656) and verified all fingerprints. Checked section 213.010 disability and section 209.200 service dog cross-references, general-law conditions in subsection 2, and premises damage liability in subsection 3. Revised subsection 4 title to name section 209.200 explicitly; retained subsections 1 to 3.

headings.title: Equal access to rented or leased housing accommodations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1977 S.B. 12, A.L. 1982 S.B. 840, A.L. 1988 H.B. 1196). Entitles blind, visually handicapped, deaf, partially deaf, and physically disabled persons to full and equal access to housing accommodations offered for rent, lease, or compensation, subject to lawful generally applicable conditions.

headings.title: Meaning and exclusions for housing accommodations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Defines 'housing accommodations' for section 209.190 and excludes single-family residences renting not more than one room as well as accommodations referenced verbatim as 'included within subsection 1 of this section' (source self-reference retained without alteration).

headings.title: No property modification or heightened duty of care required
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Clarifies that section 209.190 does not require landlords or providers to modify real property or exercise a higher degree of care for covered persons with disabilities.

headings.title: Guide, hearing, and service dogs in housing and damage liability
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Entitles blind, deaf, and physically disabled persons with guide, hearing, or service dogs to full and equal housing access without extra compensation, while holding them liable for premises damage caused by the dog.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 4 subsections and history note (L. 1977 S.B. 12 through A.L. 1988 H.B. 1196) and verified all fingerprints. Checked covered disability groups, no-modification/no-higher-duty disclaimer, guide/hearing/service dog access and damage liability, and verified the source self-referential exclusion in subsection 2 ("included within subsection 1 of this section") is documented and retained verbatim without alteration. All 4 titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: Definitions for blind literacy study section
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (subdivisions (1) to (3) and paragraphs (a) to (c)) and history note (L. 1998 H.B. 1088 § 1). Defines 'blind persons or visually impaired persons', 'literacy' (including Braille, large print, and computer-aided communications), and 'student' (referencing P.L. 94-142).

headings.title: Statewide blind student literacy study and December 1 report
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Directs the division of special education of DESE to conduct a statewide grade-level literacy study of blind students and report findings and recommendations to the governor and general assembly by December 1 each year.

headings.title: Annual implementation progress, obstacles, and plans report
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Distinguished from subsection 2 by requiring an annual December 1 report from DESE's division of special education detailing implementation progress on recommendations, significant obstacles, and plans and time frames to remove them.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 3 subsections (including subsection 1 subdivisions (1) to (3) and paragraphs (a) to (c)) and history note (L. 1998 H.B. 1088 § 1) and verified all fingerprints. Checked P.L. 94-142 reference, December 1 reporting deadlines, and distinction between the literacy study report (subsection 2) and implementation progress/obstacles report (subsection 3). All 3 titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: Causing substantial injury or death of a service dog
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (L. 2005 H.B. 116, effective 7-12-05). Makes knowingly, intentionally, or recklessly causing substantial physical injury to or death of a service dog a class A misdemeanor, with an exception for destruction for humane purposes.

headings.title: Uncontrolled animal causing injury, death, or lost function
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Makes knowingly or intentionally failing to control an owned, kept, or controlled animal to prevent substantial injury, death, or subsequent inability of a service dog to function a class A misdemeanor.

headings.title: Harassing or chasing a known service dog
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Makes harassing or chasing a dog known by the offender to be a service dog a class B misdemeanor.

headings.title: Uncontrolled animal temporarily interfering with a service dog
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Distinguished from subsection 2 by making knowing or intentional failure to control an animal from chasing or harassing a working service dog, causing temporary interference with its function, a class B misdemeanor.

headings.title: Civil action for subsection 1 or 2 violations or theft
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 (subdivisions (1) and (2)) and notes. Authorizes a service dog owner or user with a disability to sue for civil damages for a subsection 1 or 2 violation or theft resulting in loss of the dog's services. Separate review: Revised during review from "Civil action for disabling injury, death, or unrecovered theft" to reflect the exact statutory triggers (any subsection 1 or 2 violation, or theft resulting in loss of the dog's services) and distinguish cleanly from subsection 7.

headings.title: Measure of civil damages under subsection 5
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 (subdivisions (1) and (2), paragraphs (a) to (c)) and notes. Bases subsection 5 damages on replacement value of an equally trained service dog regardless of age or experience, temporary replacement service costs, reasonable theft-recovery costs, and court costs and attorney's fees.

headings.title: Civil action when an injured or stolen service dog recovers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 (subdivisions (1) and (2)) and notes. Distinguished from subsection 5 by authorizing a civil damages action where a subsection 1 to 4 violation or theft results in injury or recovery after which the dog remains able to function as a service dog.

headings.title: Measure of civil damages under subsection 7
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 (subdivisions (1) to (5)) and notes. Bases subsection 7 damages on veterinary medical expenses, retraining expenses, temporary replacement service costs, reasonable recovery costs, and court costs and attorney's fees.

headings.title: Inapplicability during criminal or civil trespass
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and notes. Renders section 209.202 inapplicable if a person with a disability, an owner, or a custodian/supervisor of a service dog commits criminal or civil trespass.

headings.title: Preservation of other legal remedies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 and notes. States that section 209.202 does not preclude any other remedies available at law.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 10 subsections (including subdivisions in subsections 5 to 8) and history/effective-date notes (L. 2005 H.B. 116; effective 7-12-05) and verified all fingerprints. Checked class A/B misdemeanor distinctions, humane-destruction exception in subsection 1, criminal/civil trespass bar in subsection 9, and contrast between subsections 5–6 and 7–8. Revised subsection 5 title to cite subsection 1 or 2 violations and theft accurately without narrowing injury or theft scope; retained other 9 titles.

headings.title: Disability impersonation for ADA service-dog accommodations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and all notes (L. 2005 H.B. 116, A.L. 2020 S.B. 644 merged with S.B. 656). Defines 'impersonates a person with a disability', makes knowing impersonation to obtain ADA (42 U.S.C. 12101 et seq.) service-dog accommodations a class C misdemeanor (class B for second or subsequent violation of this section), and imposes civil liability for actual damages.

headings.title: Misrepresenting a dog as a service dog under the ADA
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (subdivisions (1) to (4) and continuation paragraph) and notes, including footnote * noting S.B. 644 original rolls read 'shall include, but shall not be'. Prohibits knowingly misrepresenting a dog as a section 209.200 service dog for ADA accommodations, lists non-exhaustive examples, and imposes class C misdemeanor (class B for repeat subsection violations) and actual-damages civil liability.

headings.title: Misrepresenting an animal as an assistance animal
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 (subdivisions (1) to (4) and continuation paragraph) and notes, including footnote * (S.B. 644 wording) and footnote ** (S.B. 656 original rolls read 'must' rather than 'shall'). Defines 'assistance animal', prohibits knowing misrepresentation for Fair Housing Act (42 U.S.C. 3601 et seq.) or Rehabilitation Act (29 U.S.C. 701 et seq.) accommodations, requires qualified-professional documentation, and imposes class C/class B misdemeanor and actual-damages civil liability. Separate review: Revised during review from "Misrepresenting an animal as a housing assistance animal" to avoid narrowing Rehabilitation Act (29 U.S.C. 701 et seq.) coverage solely to housing.

headings.title: Online service-dog placard and business brochure
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Directs the governor's council on disability to prepare and post online a window/door placard on service dogs and Missouri misrepresentation law and a business brochure on ADA-permissible inquiries and unacceptable-behavior guidelines (retaining archived phrasing 'and as well as' without editing).

headings.title: Online landlord-tenant brochure on service dogs and assistance animals
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and notes. Directs the governor's council on disability to prepare and post online a brochure for landlords and tenants on federal and Missouri housing laws regarding service dogs and assistance animals.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 5 subsections (including subdivisions and continuation paragraphs in subsections 2 and 3) and all notes (L. 2005 H.B. 116, A.L. 2020 S.B. 644 merged with S.B. 656), including merged-bill footnotes * (S.B. 644 "shall include, but shall not be") and ** (S.B. 656 "must") and archived "and as well as" phrasing in subsection 4; verified all fingerprints. Checked section-wide vs. subsection-specific repeat-offense class B penalties and ADA, Fair Housing Act, and Rehabilitation Act references. Revised subsection 3 title to avoid limiting Rehabilitation Act assistance animals solely to housing; retained subsections 1, 2, 4, and 5.

headings.title: Aid to the blind budgeting, amount, and pension application
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1951 p. 764 § 5 through Repealed 1973 S.B. 325, A.L. 1973 H.B. 157, A.L. 2014 H.B. 1299 Revision; note historical dual repeal/amendment without claiming current enforceability). Covers family support division budgeting for federal participation, $85 plus half-excess earned-income and 12-month self-support plan disregards, the $110 monthly aid amount, and allowing disqualified persons to apply for a blind pension under sections 209.010 to 209.160.

headings.title: Pro rata reduction when aid funds are insufficient
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Directs proportional pro rata reduction of benefits under section 209.240 if funds available to the family support division become insufficient to pay full benefits.

headings.title: Medical assistance under sections 208.151 to 208.158
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Makes medical assistance payable for aid to the blind recipients as provided in sections 208.151 to 208.158 without any durational residence requirement.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 3 subsections and history note (L. 1951 p. 764 § 5 through Repealed 1973 S.B. 325, A.L. 1973 H.B. 157, A.L. 2014 H.B. 1299 Revision) and verified all fingerprints. Checked historical 1973 dual repeal/amendment note, earned-income/self-support disregards, $110 amount, pro rata reduction, and sections 208.151 to 208.158 medical assistance. Titles neutrally describe archived text without asserting current enforceability; all 3 titles retained.

headings.title: Statewide hearing aid distribution program and licensed providers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2019 S.B. 101). Directs the Missouri commission for the deaf and hard of hearing, subject to appropriations, to establish a hearing aid financial assistance program for deaf or hard-of-hearing persons at or below the federal poverty level, with assessment and distribution performed by chapter 345/346 audiologists or hearing instrument specialists or chapter 334 physicians.

headings.title: Statewide hearing aid distribution fund, restrictions, and donations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Creates the dedicated, nonreverting (exempt from section 33.080) Statewide Hearing Aid Distribution Fund under state treasurer custody and investment (sections 30.170 and 30.180), bars funding allocations from the section 161.930 assistive technology trust fund or section 209.258 deaf relay fund, and authorizes accepting private gifts, donations, grants, and bequests.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Authorizes program rulemaking by the commission subject to chapter 536 and section 536.028, with a nonseverability clause voiding rulemaking authority and rules proposed or adopted after August 28, 2019 if legislative rule-review powers are held unconstitutional.

headings.title: Contracting authority for hearing aid program
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Grants the Missouri commission for the deaf and hard of hearing permissive authority to enter into contracts, including with disability organizations, to carry out the program.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 4 subsections and history note (L. 2019 S.B. 101) and verified all fingerprints. Checked appropriations/FPL qualifications and licensed provider chapters (345, 346, 334), fund restrictions excluding sections 161.930 and 209.258 funds, section 33.080 nonreversion, and chapter 536/August 28, 2019 nonseverability clause. All 4 titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: Definitions for communication access services program
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (subdivisions (1) to (3) and paragraphs (a) to (f)) and history note (L. 2026 H.B. 1840). Defines 'commission', 'communication access services' (including section 209.285 qualified interpreters, CART, notetakers, captioning, and deaf-blind support), and 'communication access service provider'.

headings.title: Program establishment, provider registry, scholarships, and commission duties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (subdivisions (1) to (11)) and history note. Directs the commission to establish a statewide communication access services program and lists eleven duties including maintaining a regional provider registry, minimum standards, website, ADA technical assistance, outreach, appropriation-conditioned scholarships and service-request financing, hiring a fund-paid program manager, and annual reporting.

headings.title: Communication access services fund creation, uses, and investment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 (subdivisions (1) to (3)) and history note. Creates the dedicated, nonreverting (exempt from section 33.080) Communication Access Services Fund under state treasurer custody and investment (sections 30.170 and 30.180), funded by appropriations and donations for program manager salary, financial assistance, and scholarships.

headings.title: Required rulemaking and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Requires the commission to promulgate implementing rules, including scholarship distribution and financial-assistance eligibility under subsection 2(8) and (9), subject to chapter 536 and section 536.028, with nonseverability voiding rules proposed or adopted after August 28, 2026 if legislative review powers are held unconstitutional.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 4 subsections (including all subdivisions and paragraphs in subsections 1 to 3) and history note (L. 2026 H.B. 1840) and verified all fingerprints. Checked section 209.285 cross-reference, appropriation-conditioned duties in subsection 2(8)–(9), dedicated nonreverting fund in subsection 3, and mandatory rulemaking with August 28, 2026 chapter 536 nonseverability in subsection 4. All 4 titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: Statewide dual-party telecommunications relay system
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1990 H.B. 1132 § 2 merged with H.B. 1315 § 2, A.L. 1996 S.B. 525, A.L. 2000 S.B. 721). Directs the public service commission to provide a statewide dual-party relay system connecting deaf, hearing-impaired, and speech-impaired persons and representative organizations using TDDs to the telephone system.

headings.title: Statewide telecommunications equipment distribution program
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Directs the Missouri assistive technology advisory council to provide a statewide adaptive telecommunications equipment distribution program for eligible subscribers with disabilities.

headings.title: Equipment program administrator duties and spending limits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 (subdivisions (1) to (5)) and history note. Requires the equipment program administrator to provide consumer support and outreach, match equipment to individuals, offer a full range of adaptive equipment, procure cost-effectively, and spend at least 10% on support/outreach and no more than 20% on administration each fiscal year.

headings.title: Required use of Missouri organizations in contracts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Requires using Missouri public or nonpublic organizations to deliver consumer support, outreach, and administrative services in all contracts and subcontracts for the equipment distribution program.

headings.title: Designation of council as equipment program administrator
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Designates the Missouri assistive technology advisory council as the program administrator for the statewide telecommunications equipment distribution program.

headings.title: Council rulemaking authority under chapter 536
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Grants the Missouri assistive technology advisory council permissive rulemaking authority for the equipment distribution program, conditioned on promulgation under chapter 536.

headings.title: Council contracting authority for equipment program
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Authorizes the Missouri assistive technology advisory council to enter into necessary contracts, including with disability organizations, to carry out the equipment distribution program.

headings.title: No state duty to supply subscriber-premises relay equipment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history note. Clarifies that sections 209.251 to 209.259 do not require the state to purchase, install, or maintain equipment on an eligible subscriber's premises to participate in the dual-party relay system.

headings.title: No free-equipment guarantee, eligibility limits, and program scope
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and history note. Clarifies that the state need not provide adaptive equipment free to all eligible subscribers, directs the council to adopt eligibility limits based on financial means, existing access, and prior use, and limits program scope to basic telecommunications access subject to appropriations. Separate review: Revised during review from "Eligibility limits, cost-sharing, and appropriation-limited program scope" to avoid introducing "cost-sharing", which does not appear in the statute, and faithfully reflect the disclaimer of free equipment for all eligible subscribers.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 9 subsections (including subsection 3 subdivisions (1) to (5)) and history note (L. 1990 H.B. 1132 § 2 merged with H.B. 1315 § 2 through A.L. 2000 S.B. 721) and verified all fingerprints. Checked PSC vs. Missouri assistive technology advisory council roles, 10%/20% expenditure limits, chapter 536 rulemaking, premises-equipment disclaimer, and appropriation-limited scope. Revised subsection 9 title to remove unstated "cost-sharing" phrasing; retained subsections 1 to 8.

headings.title: Access-line surcharge, line cap, pay-phone exclusion, and tax exemption
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1990 H.B. 1132 § 3 subsecs. 1, 2 merged with H.B. 1315 § 3 subsecs. 1, 2 through A.L. 2000 S.B. 721). Directs the commission to establish a uniform basic telephone access-line rate recovery surcharge for section 209.253 programs, caps it at 100 lines per subscriber per location, excludes pay-phone lines, permits separate billing identification, and exempts it from chapter 144 taxes and local gross-receipts taxation.

headings.title: Subscriber payment liability and telephone company nonliability
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Makes each basic telephone access-line subscriber liable for the subsection 1 surcharge and relieves local exchange telephone companies from liability for uncollected surcharges or any duty to bring collection enforcement actions.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 1990 H.B. 1132 § 3 merged with H.B. 1315 § 3 through A.L. 2000 S.B. 721) and verified all fingerprints. Checked 100-line per-location cap, pay-phone exclusion, uniform-rate mandate, chapter 144 and local gross-receipts tax exemptions, and subscriber liability/telephone company nonliability. Both titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: Remittance of collected surcharge moneys to state treasury
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1991 S.B. 95 through A.L. 2000 S.B. 721). Requires local exchange telephone companies to pay remaining section 209.257 surcharge funds to the director of revenue as prescribed by the public service commission for remittance to the state treasurer.

headings.title: Creation and dedicated uses of deaf relay service fund
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Establishes the Deaf Relay Service and Equipment Distribution Program Fund dedicated solely to operating and administering the section 209.253 dual-party relay service and equipment distribution program and related advisory committee expenses.

headings.title: Exemption of unexpended fund balance from section 33.080
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Exempts unexpended fiscal-year balances from transfer to general revenue under section 33.080 and retains them for appropriation to the relay and equipment programs in the succeeding fiscal year.

headings.title: Annual separate line-item appropriation requests
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Requires the public service commission and the Missouri assistive technology advisory council each to annually request appropriations from the fund through separate budget line items for their respective programs.

headings.title: Conditional two-year surcharge freeze after August 28, 2000
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Prohibits increasing the surcharge rate for two years after August 28, 2000, subject to changes in federal deaf relay service requirements. Separate review: Revised during review from "Two-year surcharge rate freeze after August 28, 2000" to reflect the qualification "subject to change in federal requirements for deaf relay services".

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 5 subsections and history note (L. 1991 S.B. 95 through A.L. 2000 S.B. 721) and verified all fingerprints. Checked section 209.257 remittance, dedicated fund uses, section 33.080 exemption, separate budget line-item requests, and federal-requirements qualification on the two-year post-August 28, 2000 surcharge freeze. Revised subsection 5 title to reflect the federal-requirements condition; retained subsections 1 to 4.

headings.title: Periodic commission review and adjustment of surcharge
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1990 H.B. 1132 § 3 subsec. 4 merged with H.B. 1315 § 3 subsec. 4, A.L. 1996 S.B. 525, A.L. 2000 S.B. 721). Requires commission review of the surcharge at least every two years and no more than annually, with ordered changes as necessary to fund section 209.253 programs.

headings.title: Equipment program expenditure reports and surcharge recommendations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires annual expenditure and projection reports from the Missouri assistive technology advisory council, initial (August 28, 2000) and optional annual department surcharge recommendations based on access lines and budget, and corresponding commission surcharge revision orders under section 209.255.

headings.title: Telephone company deduction review and excess-fund surcharge suspension
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (noting official catchline ends 'excess funds, effective'). Requires concurrent commission review and adjustment of the local exchange company's section 209.257 retained deduction percentage and authorizes suspending the surcharge when excess funds are available.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 3 subsections and history note (L. 1990 H.B. 1132 § 3 subsec. 4 merged with H.B. 1315 § 3 subsec. 4 through A.L. 2000 S.B. 721) and verified all fingerprints. Checked periodic surcharge review cadence, August 28, 2000 initial and optional annual department recommendations, section 209.257 deduction review, excess-fund suspension, and official catchline ending ("excess funds, effective"). All 3 titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: Conduit status and confidentiality of facilitated conversations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1993 H.B. 600 § 2). Deems a person interpreting, transliterating, or relaying a conversation between a hearing person and a deaf person a conduit who may not disclose or be compelled by subpoena to disclose its contents without the service recipient's prior consent, except under subsection 2. Separate review: Revised during review from "Conduit status and consent required before disclosing relayed conversations" so the label covers all three statutory activities (interpreting, transliterating, and relaying) rather than solely relayed conversations.

headings.title: Court-ordered disclosure in criminal proceedings and privilege preservation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Allows courts to order conversation disclosure as evidence in proceedings related to criminal charges, while preserving legal privileges when an auxiliary aids and services provider or relay agent is used.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 1993 H.B. 600 § 2) and verified all fingerprints. Checked conduit status, subpoena protection, subsection 2 criminal-evidence disclosure exception, and privilege preservation. Revised subsection 1 title from "relayed conversations" to "facilitated conversations" to cover interpreting, transliterating, and relaying; retained subsection 2.

headings.title: Prohibition on disclosure without written permission
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1993 H.B. 600 § 3, A.L. 1995 H.B. 135). Bars an employed auxiliary aids and services provider or relay agent from disclosing contents of an interpreted, transliterated, or relayed conversation between a hearing person and a deaf or speech-impaired person without written permission from the person served.

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor penalty for unlawful disclosure
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Classifies a violation of section 209.265 as a class A misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 1993 H.B. 600 § 3, A.L. 1995 H.B. 135) and verified all fingerprints. Checked written-permission disclosure bar for auxiliary aids/services providers and relay agents serving deaf or speech-impaired persons and class A misdemeanor penalty. Both titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: Certification application forms, qualifications, oath, and nonrefundable fee
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (subdivisions (1) to (4)) and history note (L. 1994 S.B. 568 § 6 subsecs. 1, 2). Sets interpreter certification application requirements: prescribed written commission forms, proof of education/training/experience/certification and age 18 or older, oath or affirmation subject to false-declaration penalties, and nonrefundable application fee.

headings.title: Coordinator notice of evaluation or conversion date
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Directs the coordinator hired under section 209.289, upon commission receipt of an application, to notify the applicant of the earliest and most appropriate date to be evaluated or converted.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections (including subsection 1 subdivisions (1) to (4)) and history note (L. 1994 S.B. 568 § 6 subsecs. 1, 2) and verified all fingerprints. Checked age 18+ proof, oath/false-declaration statement, nonrefundable fee, and section 209.289 coordinator scheduling notice. Both titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: Interpreter evaluation competencies and communication modes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (subdivisions (1) to (6)) and history note (L. 1994 S.B. 568 § 6 subsecs. 5, 6, A.L. 2026 S.B. 890). Defines evaluation subjects (language, expressive/receptive skills, professionalism, interpreting knowledge, and ethics) and lists non-exhaustive modes of communication to be evaluated including ASL, tactile sign, language deficient, oral, Pidgin Signed English, and specialized or regional modes.

headings.title: Testing materials and confidentiality of testing records
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires the commission to use commission-developed or nationally contracted testing materials and keep all testing materials and records confidential.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections (including subsection 1 subdivisions (1) to (6)) and history note (L. 1994 S.B. 568 § 6 subsecs. 5, 6, A.L. 2026 S.B. 890) and verified all fingerprints. Checked assessed competencies, non-exhaustive communication modes, commission/national testing materials, and confidentiality mandate. Both titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: Grounds to deny, suspend, or revoke interpreter certification
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (subdivisions (1) to (6)) and history note (L. 1994 S.B. 568 § 7, A.L. 2026 S.B. 890). Authorizes the commission to suspend, deny, or revoke a certificate for impersonation, allowing certificate misuse, fraud/misrepresentation, harassing/threatening staff or evaluators, intentionally divulging confidential testing/certification material, or failing to reach a minimum satisfactory certification level.

headings.title: Chapter 621 administrative hearing procedures
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires hearings concerning certificate denial, suspension, or revocation to follow administrative hearing procedures provided in chapter 621.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections (including subsection 1 subdivisions (1) to (6)) and history note (L. 1994 S.B. 568 § 7, A.L. 2026 S.B. 890) and verified all fingerprints. Checked six permissive commission denial/suspension/revocation grounds and mandatory chapter 621 hearing procedures. Both titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: Commission fund creation, fee deposits, and disbursement limits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (L. 1994 S.B. 568 § 8, A.L. 2002 H.B. 1783, A.L. 2026 S.B. 890), including footnote * noting section 209.287 was repealed by S.B. 890, 2026. Establishes the Missouri Commission for the Deaf and Hard of Hearing Fund for fees under sections 209.287* to 209.318, limits disbursements upon appropriation to commission maintenance and enforcement, and bars paying the section 209.289 coordinator's salary from the fund.

headings.title: Biennial transfer threshold to general revenue
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Exempts the fund from section 33.080 transfers until the biennial ending balance exceeds two times the preceding fiscal year's appropriation, lapsing only the excess above that multiple.

headings.title: First fiscal year general-revenue appropriation for expenses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes, including footnote * (section 209.287 repealed by S.B. 890, 2026). Provides for paying first-fiscal-year commission maintenance and enforcement expenses under sections 209.287* to 209.318 from general revenue appropriations; retains archived wording 'maintaining the commission enforcement' verbatim without editing.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 3 subsections and notes (L. 1994 S.B. 568 § 8, A.L. 2002 H.B. 1783, A.L. 2026 S.B. 890), including footnote * noting section 209.287 was repealed by S.B. 890, 2026, and verified all fingerprints. Checked section 209.289 coordinator-salary prohibition, two-times biennial lapse threshold notwithstanding section 33.080, and archived subsection 3 phrasing ("maintaining the commission enforcement") retained without alteration. All 3 titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: Committee establishment, membership, appointment, and basic qualifications
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1994 S.B. 568 § 9, A.L. 1999 H.B. 343, A.L. 2002 H.B. 1783). Establishes the seven-member Missouri State Committee of Interpreters in the division of professional registration (including two public members, at least one deaf), appointed by the governor with senate advice and consent, requiring U.S. citizenship, Missouri residency, and interpreter licensure except as provided in subsections 2 and 3.

headings.title: Initial interpreter appointments and staggered initial terms
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires initial interpreter appointees to come from voluntarily registered interpreters with the commission and staggers initial terms across one, two, three, and four years.

headings.title: Qualifications and conflict-of-interest bars for public members
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Sets appointment qualifications for public members: U.S. citizenship, one-year Missouri residency, voter registration, never licensed under sections 209.285 to 209.339, and no past or present material financial interest in interpreting services or related organizations.

headings.title: Four-year terms, eight-year limit, and composition requirements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Establishes four-year terms, bars reappointment after eight or more years of service, requires membership reflecting diverse certification/experience/education levels, and caps interpreter educators at two.

headings.title: Vacancy appointments and removal for cause after notice and hearing
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Provides gubernatorial appointment for unexpired terms and authorizes gubernatorial removal for misconduct, inefficiency, incompetence, or neglect of duty after written notice of charges and opportunity to be heard.

headings.title: Member daily compensation cap and expense reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Authorizes committee-set daily compensation up to $50 per day devoted to committee affairs plus reimbursement of necessary and actual official expenses.

headings.title: Annual and additional meetings, officers, and quorum
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Requires an annual meeting to elect a chairperson and secretary, permits additional meetings as needed, and sets a four-member quorum.

headings.title: Staffing provided by division of professional registration
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history note. Directs the director of the division of professional registration to provide staff for the committee.

headings.title: Capacity to sue, official seal, and certified records as evidence
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and history note. Authorizes the committee to sue and be sued in its official name, requires a judicially noticed official seal, and makes sealed certified copies of committee records and division papers admissible as evidence in courts of record.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 9 subsections and history note (L. 1994 S.B. 568 § 9 through A.L. 2002 H.B. 1783) and verified all fingerprints. Checked seven-member composition, deaf public member requirement, initial staggered terms, public-member conflict bars, four-year/eight-year term limits, cause removal with notice and hearing, $50 daily compensation cap, four-member quorum, division staffing, and judicially noticed seal. All 9 titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: License requirement to practice or hold out as an interpreter
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1994 S.B. 568 § 10 through A.L. 2026 S.B. 890). Prohibits representing oneself as an interpreter or practicing interpreting as defined in section 209.285 in Missouri unless licensed under sections 209.319 to 209.339.

headings.title: Exemption for other licensed or certified professions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Excludes registered, certified, or licensed practitioners of other occupations or professions (such as physicians, psychologists, nurses, CPAs, architects, and attorneys) when performing their licensed occupation or profession.

headings.title: Limiting licensed interpreter practice to documented competence
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires licensed interpreters to restrict practice to documented areas of competence and bars practicing in untrained areas without completing an acceptable program defined by commission rule.

headings.title: Exemption for casual gratuitous or travel-incidental interpreting
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Excludes acting gratuitously as an interpreter in a casual setting as defined by rule, or interpreting incidental to traveling.

headings.title: Exemption for deaf relay telecommunications operators
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Excludes telecommunications operators providing deaf relay service or operator services for the deaf from being considered interpreting under section 209.321.

headings.title: Exemption for students in accredited interpreter degree programs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Excludes students enrolled in accredited, committee-approved degree-granting interpreter training programs while performing supervised coursework and clearly identifying themselves with a specified student, trainee, or intern title.

headings.title: Exemption for temporary out-of-state or nationally certified interpreters
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Excludes persons holding an acceptable current out-of-state license certification or national certification while temporarily in Missouri for a convention, conference, meeting, professional group, or educational field trip.

headings.title: Provisional certificate in education criteria, terms, scope, and revocation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 (subdivisions (1) to (6) and paragraphs (a) and (b)) and history note. Covers commission issuance of provisional education certificates within ten business days under two pathways, three-year and one-year terms and reevaluation-conditioned renewals, school-setting limits, and revocation grounds (noting subdivision (6) refers to revocation 'by the board' while subdivisions (1) to (4) refer to 'the commission').

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 8 subsections (including subsection 8 subdivisions (1) to (6) and paragraphs (a)–(b)) and history note (L. 1994 S.B. 568 § 10 through A.L. 2026 S.B. 890) and verified all fingerprints. Checked section 209.285 licensure scope, competence limits, five exemption categories, provisional certificate in education pathways/terms/school-setting limits, and retained source discrepancy in subsection 8(6) referring to revocation "by the board" while subdivisions (1)–(4) cite "the commission". All 8 titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: License application contents, certifications, oath, fee, and minimum age
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1994 S.B. 568 § 11, A.L. 2002 H.B. 1783, A.L. 2004 S.B. 1122). Requires division application forms, proof of education and qualifying RID/NAD/Missouri certification, oath or affirmation subject to false-declaration penalties under sections 209.319 to 209.339, nonrefundable fee, and age 18 or older.

headings.title: License expiration, renewal notice, denial, and two-year reinstatement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Sets license expiration on the renewal date, requires mailed renewal notices, allows expiration and denial for failure to provide renewal proof or fees within sixty days, and permits reinstatement within two years with renewal and delinquency fees plus proof of current certification.

headings.title: Issuance or renewal upon compliance with application requirements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Directs the committee with division assistance, except as provided in section 209.321, to issue or renew a license to applicants submitting required applications, fees, and satisfactory evidence of subsection 1 or 2 compliance.

headings.title: Replacement of lost, destroyed, or mutilated licenses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Grants the committee permissive authority to issue a replacement license upon payment of a committee-provided fee.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 4 subsections and history note (L. 1994 S.B. 568 § 11 through A.L. 2004 S.B. 1122) and verified all fingerprints. Checked RID/NAD/Missouri certification proof, oath, nonrefundable fee, age 18 minimum, 60-day expiration/denial and two-year reinstatement window, section 209.321 exception on issuance/renewal, and permissive replacement licensing. All 4 titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: Permissive fingerprint requirement for interpreter and temporary licenses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2025 S.B. 71 merged with S.B. 81 & 174). Authorizes ('may require') the state committee of interpreters to require fingerprint submissions as part of applications for section 209.285 interpreter or section 209.326 temporary interpreter licensure.

headings.title: Conditional fingerprint submission to Missouri State Highway Patrol
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires the committee, if it exercises subsection 1 authority, to have applicants submit fingerprints to the Missouri state highway patrol for state and federal criminal history background checks. Separate review: Revised during review from "Submission of fingerprints to Missouri State Highway Patrol" to reflect that highway patrol submission is conditioned on the committee exercising its permissive subsection 1 authority.

headings.title: State and FBI criminal record searches and committee access
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Directs submission of fingerprints and fees to the highway patrol central repository for state searches and FBI forwarding under section 43.540, notification to the committee of results, and committee access to discovered criminal history records notwithstanding section 610.120.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 3 subsections and history note (L. 2025 S.B. 71 merged with S.B. 81 & 174) and verified all fingerprints. Checked permissive ("may require") fingerprint authority for section 209.285 interpreter and section 209.326 temporary interpreter applicants, conditional highway patrol submission, FBI search under section 43.540, and committee access notwithstanding section 610.120. Revised subsection 2 title to reflect its conditional trigger; retained subsections 1 and 3.

headings.title: General chapter 536 rulemaking and ethical rules of conduct
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1994 S.B. 568 § 13). Authorizes the committee to adopt rules carrying out sections 209.319 to 209.339 in accordance with chapter 536, including promulgating 'Ethical Rules of Conduct' governing interpreter practices.

headings.title: Specific rulemaking subjects including applications, fees, and reciprocity
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (subdivisions (1) to (5)) and history note. Lists non-exhaustive committee rulemaking subjects: initial/renewal/temporary license applications, fees, recognized qualifying credentials, complaint and violation investigation/resolution procedures, and interstate reciprocity policies.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections (including subsection 2 subdivisions (1) to (5)) and history note (L. 1994 S.B. 568 § 13) and verified all fingerprints. Checked chapter 536 rulemaking requirement, Ethical Rules of Conduct authority, and non-exhaustive list of application, fee, credential, complaint, and reciprocity rule subjects. Both titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: State committee of interpreters fund creation and disbursement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1994 S.B. 568 §§ 15, 16). Establishes the State Committee of Interpreters Fund for fees under sections 209.319 to 209.339 collected by the division director and transmitted via the department of revenue, disbursable upon appropriation only for committee maintenance and enforcement.

headings.title: Biennial transfer thresholds to general revenue
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Exempts the fund from section 33.080 transfer until the biennial ending balance exceeds two times the preceding fiscal year's appropriation (or three times if license renewal is less frequent than annual), lapsing only the excess. Separate review: Verified source wording refers to "the board" ("if the board requires by rule license renewal less frequently than yearly") despite the licensing body being "the committee"; retained without silent alteration.

headings.title: Exemption of licensed interpreters from municipal taxes and license fees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Prohibits imposing any municipal or other corporation tax or license fee on committee-licensed interpreters for the privilege of practicing the profession.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 3 subsections and history note (L. 1994 S.B. 568 §§ 15, 16) and verified all fingerprints. Checked dedicated fund disbursements, two-times/three-times biennial transfer thresholds notwithstanding section 33.080 (noting archived reference to "the board" in subsection 2 despite "the committee" elsewhere, retained without alteration), and municipal tax/license fee exemption. All 3 titles retained as accurate; added "the board" source-wording note to subsection 2.

headings.title: Refusal to issue or renew license and appeal notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1994 S.B. 568 § 17, A.L. 2002 H.B. 1783, A.L. 2020 H.B. 2046). Authorizes refusing issuance or renewal for subsection 2 causes and requires written notice of reasons and of the applicant's right to file a chapter 621 complaint with the administrative hearing commission.

headings.title: Administrative hearing commission complaints and fourteen disciplinary causes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (subdivisions (1) to (14)) and history note. Authorizes filing chapter 621 complaints against current, non-renewed, or surrendered licensees and lists fourteen causes including substance impairment, section 324.012 directly related criminal offenses, fraud, incompetency, rule violations, impersonation, out-of-state or certifying-body discipline, incapacity, aiding unlicensed practice, material mistake, breach of trust, and license-display failures.

headings.title: Civil immunity for good-faith reports to committee
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Protects persons, organizations, associations, or corporations reporting or providing information to the committee in good faith under sections 209.319 to 209.339 from civil damages actions.

headings.title: Chapter 621 hearings and disciplinary sanctions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Requires chapter 621 proceedings after complaint filing and authorizes the committee, upon an administrative hearing commission finding of subsection 2 grounds, to censure, place on probation up to five years, suspend up to three years, or revoke a license.

headings.title: Optional three-year waiting period after license revocation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Grants the committee permissive authority in a revocation order to bar reinstatement applications for three years after revocation.

headings.title: Certification verification required before restoring license
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Requires committee verification from the 'Missouri commission for the deaf' (archived agency name retained) of current qualifying certification before restoring a revoked, suspended, or inactive license to good standing.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 6 subsections (including subsection 2 subdivisions (1) to (14)) and history note (L. 1994 S.B. 568 § 17 through A.L. 2020 H.B. 2046) and verified all fingerprints. Checked chapter 621 refusal notice and complaint procedures, fourteen disciplinary causes (including section 324.012 criminal offenses), good-faith reporting immunity, probation/suspension/revocation limits, permissive three-year revocation bar, and archived "Missouri commission for the deaf" reference in subsection 6. All 6 titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor penalty for statutory violations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1994 S.B. 568 § 18). Makes a violation of any provision of sections 209.319 to 209.339 a class A misdemeanor.

headings.title: Required refund of fees received in violation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires refunding all fees or other compensation received for services rendered in violation of sections 209.319 to 209.339.

headings.title: Committee power to sue and department enforcement duty
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Authorizes the committee to sue in its own name in any Missouri court and directs the department to inquire diligently into violations, institute penalty actions, and generally enforce sections 209.319 to 209.339.

headings.title: Attorney general injunctive actions for unlicensed practice or serious harm
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 (subdivisions (1) and (2)) and history note. Permits the attorney general, upon committee application, to seek injunctions or restraining orders against unlicensed practice/offers or licensed practice presenting a substantial probability of serious harm to a resident or client.

headings.title: Venue for enforcement actions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Requires commencing section 209.337 actions either in the county where the conduct occurred or where the defendant resides.

headings.title: Cumulative and concurrent nature of enforcement actions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Allows bringing section 209.337 actions in addition to, in lieu of, or concurrently with other penalties or enforcement actions under sections 209.319 to 209.339.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 6 subsections (including subsection 4 subdivisions (1) and (2)) and history note (L. 1994 S.B. 568 § 18) and verified all fingerprints. Checked class A misdemeanor penalty, mandatory fee refunds, committee standing and department enforcement duties, attorney general injunction triggers, county venue, and cumulative/concurrent remedies. All 6 titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: Interpreter conduit status and confidentiality of conversations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1994 S.B. 568 § 19). Deems an interpreter of a hearing-deaf conversation a conduit barred from disclosing or being compelled by subpoena to disclose conversation contents without the service recipient's prior consent, subject to subsections 2 to 4.

headings.title: Court-ordered criminal disclosure and preservation of legal privileges
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Authorizes court-ordered disclosure as evidence in proceedings related to criminal charges while preserving legally privileged communications when an interpreter is used.

headings.title: Disclosure exception for licensee disciplinary proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Exempts licensee disciplinary investigations, hearings, and proceedings from the disclosure bar and prohibits licensees from withholding relevant records or testimony on confidentiality grounds.

headings.title: Disclosure exception for unlicensed-practice proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Removes the disclosure prohibition and refusal right for any person, licensed or unlicensed, in proceedings related to allegations of practicing interpreting without a license.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 4 subsections and history note (L. 1994 S.B. 568 § 19) and verified all fingerprints. Checked interpreter conduit confidentiality with subsections 2 to 4 exceptions, criminal-proceeding court orders preserving legal privileges, disciplinary-proceeding exception, and unlicensed-practice allegation exception. All 4 titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: ABLE program creation, board composition, terms, and ethics removal
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2015 S.B. 174 § 166.605, A.L. 2016 H.B. 2125). Creates the Missouri ABLE Program administered by the seven-member Missouri ABLE board (treasurer as chair, three department/OA heads or designees, two legislative-leader appointees, and one senate-confirmed gubernatorial appointee), sets four-year appointed terms, and mandates removal for violating section 105.452.

headings.title: Enumerated powers and authority of the ABLE board
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (subdivisions (1) to (13)) and history note. Lists thirteen board powers including developing the program, rulemaking for 26 U.S.C. Section 529A qualification, participant education, institutional and interstate agreements, participation agreements, accepting grants/appropriations, investing funds, distributions, refunds, administration costs, and insurance.

headings.title: Board quorum, majority voting, and proxy limits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Sets a four-member quorum unaffected by vacancies, requires a majority vote of members present for action, and allows single-meeting voting proxies with no more than three proxies counting toward quorum.

headings.title: Quarterly board meetings, notice, and unanimous consent
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Requires meeting within Missouri at least once per quarter as scheduled or requested by four members, requires six-day personal or mailed notice, and permits meeting at any time by unanimous mutual consent.

headings.title: Prudent investment standard, counselor delegation, and fiduciary protection
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Incorporates the section 105.688 prudent-person standard, directs studying other states' plans for contracts after August 28, 2015, allows delegating investment authority to SEC-registered investment counselors, and shields board members acting in good faith with ordinary business care and prudence from liability.

headings.title: Conflict-of-interest ban on board member investment dealings
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Prohibits handling board-authorized investment transactions through firms in which a board member has a substantial interest and bars board members from profiting directly or indirectly from such investments.

headings.title: Prohibition on personal gain and bribery penalties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Distinguished from subsection 6 by barring any board member or ABLE program employee from gaining or profiting from program funds or transactions, and imposing office forfeiture and bribery penalties on members, employees, or agents accepting gratuities or compensation to influence investment or management actions.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 7 subsections (including subsection 2 subdivisions (1) to (13)) and history note (L. 2015 S.B. 174 § 166.605, A.L. 2016 H.B. 2125) and verified all fingerprints.
