headings.title: Participation agreement authority and required disclosures
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (subdivisions (1) to (5)) and history note (L. 2015 S.B. 174 § 166.610 through A.L. 2021 H.B. 297). Authorizes participation agreements under sections 209.600 to 209.645 and requires stipulating program terms, return-calculation methods, prominent risk disclosures, plain public language, and prominent disclosure of load or administrative charges.

headings.title: Annual contribution limit aligned with 26 U.S.C. 529A
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Directs the board to set the annual ABLE account contribution maximum equal to the amount allowed under 26 U.S.C. Section 529A.

headings.title: Total account balance limit and excess-contribution safeguards
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires a total beneficiary contribution limit at least as high as the Missouri education program board's limit under sections 166.400 to 166.450, bars contributions causing balances to exceed that limit, and permits additional safeguards against exceeding qualified disability expense needs.

headings.title: Minimum holding period for tax exemption and early-withdrawal penalty
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Directs the board to establish the minimum holding period for section 209.625 tax-exempt treatment and subjects earlier withdrawals or distributions to a penalty under section 209.620.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 4 subsections (including subsection 1 subdivisions (1) to (5)) and history note (L. 2015 S.B. 174 § 166.610 through A.L. 2021 H.B. 297) and verified all fingerprints. Checked required participation-agreement disclosures, 26 U.S.C. 529A annual limit, sections 166.400 to 166.450 total-limit floor, and minimum holding period with section 209.625/209.620 tax-exemption and penalty cross-references. All 4 titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: State and local tax exemption and income tax deduction
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2015 S.B. 174 § 166.625, A.L. 2019 S.B. 230). Exempts qualifying ABLE program and account assets and income from state and local taxation and chapter 143 income tax (excluding non-program expenditures), and allows subtracting annual contributions up to $8,000 per taxpayer ($16,000 married filing jointly) from Missouri adjusted gross income under section 143.121.

headings.title: Tax recapture for nonqualified or early distributions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires adding back distributed deductible contributions or earnings to the Missouri adjusted gross income of the participant (or designated beneficiary if participant is deceased) when not used for qualified disability expenses or not held for the board-set minimum period.

headings.title: Tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2015
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Specifies that section 209.625 applies to tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2015.

headings.title: Exclusion of ABLE assets from chapter 475 conservatorship estates
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. States that ABLE account assets under sections 209.600 to 209.645 are not considered property of a conservatorship estate established under chapter 475.

headings.title: Exception for accounts held by a public administrator
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Exempts ABLE accounts in the charge and custody of a public administrator from the subsection 4 conservatorship-estate exclusion.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 5 subsections and history note (L. 2015 S.B. 174 § 166.625, A.L. 2019 S.B. 230) and verified all fingerprints. Checked state/local and chapter 143 tax exemptions, $8,000/$16,000 section 143.121 subtraction, nonqualified/early distribution add-back to participant or beneficiary, January 1, 2015 tax-year effective date, chapter 475 conservatorship exclusion, and public-administrator carve-out. All 5 titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: Short title of Missouri Employment First Act
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2023 S.B. 45 & 90 merged with S.B. 106). Designates section 209.700 as the 'Missouri Employment First Act'.

headings.title: Definitions for Employment First Act
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (subdivisions (1) to (13), including nested paragraphs and clauses) and history note. Defines thirteen terms including competitive integrated employment (citing 29 U.S.C. 206(a)(1)), customized employment, ADA-based disability (excluding brief intoxication or substance addiction), employment first, employment-related services, integrated setting, outcome, section 178.900 sheltered workshop, state agency, supported employment and services, working age (16+), and youth with a disability (14 to under 18).

headings.title: Interagency memorandums of understanding and coordinated employment strategies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 (subdivisions (1) and (2)) and history note. Directs state agencies providing employment-related or disability services to enter collaborative written memorandums of understanding and implement coordinated strategies promoting competitive integrated employment.

headings.title: Agency duties on Employment First policy, information, training, and youth
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 (subdivisions (1) to (9)) and history note. Lists nine state agency obligations: adopting Employment First as first preferred outcome, offering working-age benefit/ABLE/assistive-technology information, exploring education pathways (without requiring funding unless required by law), promoting individualized training and private/employer partnerships, supporting school/provider staff, ensuring employment is not required to keep public benefits, and holding annual discussions with parents, guardians, or emancipated youth.

headings.title: No interference with federal statutory duties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Clarifies that section 209.700 does not require any state agency action interfering with fulfillment of duties and requirements mandated by federal law.

headings.title: Preservation of disability benefits when unable to work competitively
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Clarifies that section 209.700 does not limit or disallow disability benefits for a person with a disability who is unable to engage in competitive integrated employment.

headings.title: Retention of supported employment and sheltered workshop options
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Clarifies that section 209.700 does not eliminate supported employment services or sheltered workshop settings as options.

headings.title: No hiring preference required and state minimum job qualifications
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 (subdivisions (1) and (2)) and history note. Clarifies that section 209.700 neither requires hiring preferences nor prohibits otherwise lawful employment relationships or programs, and requires state agency employees to meet minimum position qualifications.

headings.title: Ongoing agency coordination, data sharing, and measurable goals
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and history note. Distinguished from subsections 3 and 4 by directing ongoing coordination across state agencies, feasible cross-system data and information sharing to track implementation progress, and encouraging adoption of measurable goals and objectives.

headings.title: Agency rulemaking authority and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 and history note. Grants state agencies permissive rulemaking authority subject to chapter 536 and section 536.028, with a nonseverability clause voiding rulemaking authority and rules proposed or adopted after August 28, 2023 if legislative rule-review powers are held unconstitutional.
